function.name: telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get
function.description: Retrieves specified telemetry information for a network interface within a given fabric, node, and pod, filtered by the interface and information types. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit the nodes pertaining to the given fabric name.

nodeId.description: The identifier of the node to limit the results pertaining to the given node ID.

podId.description: The identifier of the pod to limit the results pertaining to the given pod ID.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit the results pertaining to the given interface type.

infoType.description: The type of information to retrieve about the interface.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide showing **exactly** what you need to do to pull data for a specific interface using the `telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get` helper. --- ### 1️⃣ What You Need To Know First | Parameter | Type | Meaning | |-----------|------|---------| | `fabricName` | *String* | Name of the fabric whose nodes you’re interested in (`“prod-fabric”`, `"test"` …). | | `nodeId` | *Number* | Unique numeric ID of the switch/node inside that fabric. | | `podId` | *Number* | Pod/cluster grouping – often used when your fabric spans multiple pods. | | `interfaceType` | *Enum* | One of four supported interface families:
• `"svi"`
• `"ethernet"`
• `"loopback"`
• `"port-channel"` | | `infoType` | *Enum* | Which slice of data you want back:
• `"interfaces"` – basic config & attributes
• `"status"` – operational state (up/down, speed)
• `"statistics"` – counters (packets, bytes…)
• `"errors"` – error counts | All five arguments are required; missing one will cause the request to fail. --- ### 2️⃣ Example Call (Python) ```python from functions import telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get result = telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get( fabricName="core-prod", # <-- change as appropriate nodeId=101, # <-- replace with real node id podId=0, # <-- usually 0 unless multi‑pod interfaceType="ethernet", # could also be svi / loopback / port-channel infoType="statistics" # pick whichever view you need ) print(result) ``` #### Expected Output Structure (Actual keys depend on `infoType`; here’s a typical “statistics” payload): ```json { "fabric": "core-prod", "node_id": 101, "pod_id": 0, "interface_type": "ethernet", "data": [ { "name": "Ethernet1/1", "in_octets": 123456789, "out_octets": 987654321, "in_packets": 54321, "out_packets": 12345, ... }, ... more interfaces ... ] } ``` If you requested `"status"`, you’ll see fields like: ```json { "name":"Ethernet1/1", "oper_status":"up", "speed_mbps":10000, "duplex":"full" } ``` --- ### 3️⃣ Quick Checklist Before Calling | ✅ Check | Why it matters | |----------|----------------| | Fabric exists & spelled correctly | Avoid lookup errors | | Node ID belongs to that fabric | Guarantees correct device context | | Interface type matches actual hardware | Prevents empty result sets | | Info type chosen based on your goal | Saves bandwidth & processing time | --- ### 4️⃣ Common Pitfalls & Fixes | Symptom | Likely Cause | Remedy | |--------|--------------|-------| | Empty list returned | Wrong `nodeId` or no matching interfaces | Verify node ID via inventory query | | Error “invalid interface type” | Misspelled value or unsupported family | Use exact enum strings shown above | | Timeout / slow response | Large fabric + many interfaces | Narrow scope: filter by `interfaceType` or add additional filters if available | --- ### 5️⃣ Next Steps After Retrieval Once you’ve got the raw JSON, you can: - Store it in a database for trend analysis. - Feed it into Grafana dashboards. - Trigger alerts if certain thresholds exceed limits. Feel free to let me know which part you'd like deeper help with—whether it's parsing the JSON, automating repeated pulls, or visualizing the stats!
